tei:bibl.tei:title: אֲדוֹן עוֹלָם (מנהג הספרדים במזרח)
Adōn Olam (Ladino translation from the Sidur Tefilat Kol Pe, 1891)
tei:bibl.tei:author: Shlomo ibn Gabirol
tei:bibl.tei:note: Converted from the export of opensiddur.org at 624215eef0.

tei:div.tei:p: The Seder Tefilat Kol Peh was printed in 1891 in Vienna, and features a full Ladino translation of the entire siddur. This Ladino translation of Adon Olam is found on the left side of pagespread No145. Along with a full transcription of the Ladino text, Isaac Gantwerk Mayer has also prepared a full romanization of the Ladino. I have set the Hebrew text of Adon Olam side-by-side with the Ladino.

Adon Olam is a piyyut that became popular in the 15th century and is often attributed to Solomon ibn Gabirol (1021–1058) and less often to Sherira Gaon (900-1001), or his son, Hai ben Sherira Gaon (939-1038). The variation of the piyyut appearing here is the sixteen-line version familiar to Eastern Sepharadi congregations.
